title: Texting 911: How It Works in the US and Canada #shorts
summary: In 2021, 38 US states reported 507,969 texts to 911. In Canada, Text with 9-1-1 is for registered people who are deaf, hard of hearing or speech impaired.
sources: 2021 data: 45 states reported 213,652,929 total 911 calls; 49 states reported 4,637 primary PSAPs; 38 states reported 507,969 texts to 911 (NHTSA National 911 Program, National 911 Annual Report: 2021 Data): https://www.911.gov/assets/2021-911-Profile-Database-Report_FINAL.pdf

The US 911 system is operated by local and state government; where text-to-911 is not available, the sender gets a bounce-back message (911.gov, Frequently asked questions): https://911.gov/calling-911/frequently-asked-questions

Text with 9-1-1 (T9-1-1) is only for deaf, deafened, hard of hearing or speech impaired persons, who must register with their wireless provider (Text with 9-1-1, history): https://www.textwith911.ca/en/history/

scenes.narration: In {2021|twenty twenty-one}, {38|thirty-eight} states reported over half a million texts to {911|nine one one}.
In Canada, texting {9-1-1|nine one one} is for people who are deaf, hard of hearing or speech impaired. They register, then the call continues by text.
Two countries, two different rules for texting.
